result.title: CohortFlow: A Steerable Clinical Cohort Curation Agent with Localized Semantic Correction
result.summary: Language model agents for clinical cohort curation should accommodate evolving eligibility criteria without repeatedly processing unchanged requirements. We introduce CohortFlow, a steerable agent that represents natural language corrections as localized updates to a structured cohort specification and reconciles them with a persistent execution graph. Explicitly recorded semantic dependencies enable affected computations to be selectively invalidated while preserving valid prior results. On 100 scenarios derived from clinical-trial eligibility criteria, comprising 126 correction turns, localized steering achieves 77.0% requirement micro-F1 versus 76.4% for full regeneration using the same 8B model, a small numerical advantage that is not statistically significant ($p=0.493$). It reduces mean correction latency by 64.8% after completion and 44.3% during execution, with 38.1% fewer model calls. In a separate proof-of-concept evaluation over MIMIC, all 13 cohort states execute successfully, while correction trajectories demonstrate selective preservation of unaffected computations and recomputation of changed or dependent nodes. Together, these results show that localized semantic steering can substantially reduce correction latency and model calls while maintaining strong requirement-level accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CohortFlow，一个可操控的临床队列筛选 agent：把自然语言修正解析为对结构化队列规格的局部更新，并借助持久执行图与显式语义依赖，只失效受影响的计算、保留其余结果；在 100 个试验入排标准场景上验证精度、延迟与调用次数变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基于依赖记录的选择性失效与增量重算机制，可能与 LVR 中推理状态的局部更新、动态计算预算分配及缓存复用问题相通，可供核查其「更新—失效—重算」粒度能否迁移到 latent 或轨迹级状态更新；但无视觉多模态内容，纯属方法线索。
